READ FIRST:
- src/components/atlas/AtlasSection.tsx (the E5 surface you extend: it already computes baseline and shocked scenario summaries and renders StormAtlas cells plus AtlasStripPlot; find how it gets the current twist and scenario label), src/components/atlas/StormAtlas.tsx, src/lib/stormAtlas.ts (state union, summarizeStormAtlas, scenarioLabel contract), src/lib/weatherState.ts (7-state ladder and the state colors/tokens), src/components/atlas/atlas.css (existing styles, extend here), src/lib/shockPresets.ts (preset ids), src/index.css (reduced motion pattern, design tokens), src/lib/format.ts (formatCents), src/dashScan.test.ts (your new files must satisfy the dash scan: no em dashes, en dashes, double hyphens in any file).

FIXED SCHEMA of public/data/engine/atlas.json (backend is writing this right now):
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generated_by": "scripts.engine.build",
  "states": ["clear","cloudy","overcast","rain","drought","storm","flood"],
  "districts": [{"district_id": 1, "district_name": "...", "region": "...", "inhabitants": 12345, "unemployment_rate_2023": 4.5 or null, "average_salary": 15000 or null, "account_count": 60, "no_data": false}],
  "account_district": {"<account_id>": district_id},
  "baseline": {"<district_id>": {"clear": 10, "cloudy": 12, "overcast": 0, "rain": 8, "drought": 5, "storm": 3, "flood": 2}},
  "scenarios": {"<preset_id>": {"<district_id>": {same 7-state counts}}}
}

WHAT TO BUILD:

1. src/lib/atlasData.ts (new) + atlasData.test.ts: strict loader for atlas.json (same refusal style as src/data/profiles.ts: name every refusing field, reject schema drift), typed exports (AtlasDoc, DistrictRow, StateCounts), helpers: districtSeverity(district counts) -> severity share (storm + flood over account_count, or a documented severity-weighted metric: pick ONE, document it in a code comment and in the legend), binFor(share) -> one of 5 shading bins, regionsGrouped(doc) -> districts grouped by region name sorted alphabetically within region. Fixture atlas.json inline in tests (7 districts across 3 regions including one no_data district).

2. src/components/atlas/Cartogram.tsx (new) + Cartogram.test.tsx: 77 district tiles rendered as a grid grouped into region bands (each band labeled with its region name). Each tile: district_name (small), share or count (tabular numerals), background shaded by its bin using the existing weather state colors (--wx- tokens or the atlas palette already in atlas.css). no_data tiles render with an explicit "no data" pattern (diagonal hatch or muted cross), never a zero shade. Tiles are keyboard focusable buttons with aria-label like "District Prague-sever, 12 of 60 accounts in storm or flood". Clicking a tile calls an optional onSelectDistrict callback (wire nothing for now beyond console-free typed callback; drill-down comes later if time). Legend printed below the grid: the 5 bins with ranges, "one tile is one district, arranged by region, not to geography", and the severity share definition verbatim. Motion: when the scenario (twist) changes, tile colors transition over 600ms ease-out ONLY under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (the cascade money-shot moment: colors sweep across tiles). Reduced motion: instant swap. The component reads counts, never recomputes them.

3. src/components/atlas/RainGauge.tsx (new) + RainGauge.test.tsx: a vertical pixel rain gauge (SVG) whose fill = share of accounts NOT in storm or flood under the current scenario (document this definition on the gauge face: "share of accounts outside storm and flood"). Exact percentage printed in large tabular numerals on the glass, plus the raw count "3,412 of 4,500". Fill animates height 600ms under no-preference only. A printed danger line at 80 percent outside-storm share (or document your chosen threshold as a design constant). Reads counts from the same summary the AtlasSection already computes (props in, no data fetching inside the component).

4. Mount both into src/components/atlas/AtlasSection.tsx: Cartogram above or below the existing StormAtlas grid (your call on layout, keep the seven-cell grid visible as the counts backbone per user decision), RainGauge beside the headline. AtlasSection already reacts to the active twist, so cartogram tiles and gauge fill must move together with the cells when the scenario changes. Do not remove or weaken any existing AtlasSection behavior or test.

5. atlas.css: extend with cartogram and gauge styles using existing tokens only (--wx- state colors, --cp- or atlas tokens already there). No new raw hex outside the established palette. Responsive: cartogram grid uses auto-fit minmax so it works on 1366 laptop and 1080p projector; bump label sizes at large viewports.

HONESTY RULES (non-negotiable): every number displayed comes from atlas.json or props; the legend prints the severity definition and the region-not-geography caveat; no_data never renders as 0; scenario labels come from the existing scenarioLabel contract; reduced motion path exists for every animation; no network calls.

FILES YOU OWN (create/modify only these): src/lib/atlasData.ts, src/lib/atlasData.test.ts, src/components/atlas/Cartogram.tsx, src/components/atlas/Cartogram.test.tsx, src/components/atlas/RainGauge.tsx, src/components/atlas/RainGauge.test.tsx, src/components/atlas/AtlasSection.tsx (mount + layout only), src/components/atlas/atlas.css (append), and if needed src/lib/weatherState.test.ts may gain a test asserting the weather state fixture table scripts/engine/weather_state_goldens.json (backend is generating that file with hand-derived expected values from the TS ladder; if the file does not exist yet, skip that one test with a clear skip and note it).

DO NOT TOUCH: src/lib/judgeMode*, src/components/judge/, src/state/ (another agent owns E6 judge mode), src/lib/shockParse*, src/components/console/TypedShock* (Gemini path), scripts/, README, App.tsx, docs/.

TESTS: all new tests must pass with inline fixtures (no dependency on the real atlas.json landing). Run npx vitest run on your files plus src/components/atlas/ and src/dashScan.test.ts, and npm run typecheck. Also run npx vitest run src/app.smoke.test.ts to confirm the App still renders. Report exact counts. Do not run the full suite (other agents are mid-edit).

1: import type { AccountProfile } from '../data/profiles'
2: import { SHOCK_PRESETS } from './shockPresets'
3: import {
4:   IDLE_TWIST,
5:   RUNWAY_CAP_DECI_MONTHS,
6:   applyTwist,
7:   normalizeTwist,
8:   roundHalfUp,
9:   sameTwist,
10:   type RunwayState,
11:   type Twist,
12: } from './shocks'
13: import { VERDICT_BANDS, verdictBand, type VerdictBandId } from './verdict'
14: 
15: /**
16:  * Phase E5 Storm Atlas aggregation: count a population of accounts by
17:  * verdict band under one twist, and build the headline the pitch opens
18:  * with, for example "10% of accounts would have under 3 months of
19:  * runway under the laid off twist".
20:  *
21:  * The fold is done in this file: the seven state ladder in
22:  * src/lib/weatherState.ts is deleted, and verdict.ts owns every band
23:  * id, label, glyph, and threshold. The atlas counts, the console
24:  * badge, and the forecast strip therefore read one vocabulary and can
25:  * never disagree about where a band boundary sits.
26:  *
27:  * Honesty rule, structural: scenario wording enters a summary only
28:  * through shockedAtlasScenario, the same call that ran applyTwist over
29:  * every profile, so a sentence can never claim a twist the numbers did
30:  * not run. AtlasSection is the production caller and passes the pair
31:  * together.
32:  *
33:  * Pure module: no React, no fetch, no artifact reads. Counts are
34:  * integers, whole percents come from roundHalfUp and may not sum to
35:  * 100, and no float ever decides a branch.
36:  */
37: 
38: /** One atlas row: an account id plus the runway answer it lands on. */
39: export interface AtlasEntry {
40:   account_id: string
41:   runway_state: RunwayState
42:   runway_deci_months: number
43: }
44: 
45: /** Count or percent per band, keyed by the canonical band union. */
46: export type BandCounts = Record<VerdictBandId, number>
47: 
48: export type BandPercents = Record<VerdictBandId, number>
49: 
50: /** Ladder order, lowest runway first, straight from verdict.ts. */
51: export const ATLAS_BAND_ORDER: readonly VerdictBandId[] = VERDICT_BANDS.map((band) => band.id)
52: 
53: /** The headline counts the two bands under the confirmed threshold. */
54: export const DEFAULT_HEADLINE_BANDS: readonly VerdictBandId[] = ['critical', 'storm_warning']
55: 
56: /** The user confirmed headline threshold, in plain words (docs/decisions.md). */
57: export const DEFAULT_HEADLINE_THRESHOLD_WORDS = '3 months'
58: 
59: /** Default scenario wording: only a caller that ran a twist says otherwise. */
60: export const DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL = 'at baseline'
61: 
62: export interface StormAtlasSummary {
63:   /** Entries counted, the population under the caller's scenario. */
64:   total: number
65:   /** Accounts per band, integers. */
66:   counts: BandCounts
67:   /** Whole percent per band, roundHalfUp, may not sum to 100. */
68:   percents: BandPercents
69:   /** The bands the headline speaks about. */
70:   headlineBands: readonly VerdictBandId[]
71:   /** The threshold sentence the headline quotes, for example 3 months. */
72:   headlineThresholdWords: string
73:   /** Accounts across those bands. */
74:   headlineCount: number
75:   /** Whole percent of the population in those bands. */
76:   headlinePercent: number
77:   /** "1 in N" over the whole population, null when the count is 0. */
78:   oneInN: number | null
79:   /** The working sentence, ready to render. */
80:   headline: string
81:   /** What the numbers ran under, printed at the end of the headline. */
82:   scenarioLabel: string
83: }
84: 
85: export interface StormAtlasOptions {
86:   /** Bands the headline reports, default the two under 3 months. */
87:   headlineBands?: readonly VerdictBandId[]
88:   /** Threshold words the headline quotes, default 3 months. */
89:   headlineThresholdWords?: string
90:   /**
91:    * Scenario suffix, default the honest baseline wording. Callers pass
92:    * scenario.scenarioLabel from shockedAtlasScenario, never prose of
93:    * their own, which is what keeps the sentence honest by construction.
94:    */
95:   scenarioLabel?: string
96: }
97: 
98: /** All zero counts, in canonical ladder order. */
99: export function emptyBandCounts(): BandCounts {
100:   const counts = {} as BandCounts
101:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_ORDER) {
102:     counts[band] = 0
103:   }
104:   return counts
105: }
106: 
107: function emptyBandPercents(): BandPercents {
108:   const percents = {} as BandPercents
109:   for (const band of ATLAS_BAND_ORDER) {
110:     percents[band] = 0
111:   }
112:   return percents
113: }
114: 
115: /**
116:  * Clamp one runway reading to the artifact range the E1 loader
117:  * enforces (0 to 1200 tenths). A non finite reading reads 0, which
118:  * lands on Critical: unknown data must never render as clear skies.
119:  */
120: export function clampDeciMonths(raw: number): number {
121:   if (!Number.isFinite(raw)) {
122:     return 0
123:   }
124:   return Math.min(RUNWAY_CAP_DECI_MONTHS, Math.max(0, raw))
125: }
126: 
127: /**
128:  * One entry's band through the single verdict vocabulary: the two
129:  * special runway states are decided before any threshold, exactly as
130:  * verdictBand reads a RunwayAnswer, so an atlas count can never
131:  * disagree with the badge next to it.
132:  */
133: export function entryBand(entry: AtlasEntry): VerdictBandId {
134:   return verdictBand({
135:     state: entry.runway_state,
136:     deciMonths: clampDeciMonths(entry.runway_deci_months),
137:   }).id
138: }
139: 
140: /**
141:  * Count a population once. Null, undefined, and empty arrays
142:  * aggregate to a zero summary with an honest placeholder headline, so
143:  * the atlas can mount before the loader resolves.
144:  */
145: export function summarizeStormAtlas(
146:   entries: readonly AtlasEntry[] | null | undefined,
147:   options: StormAtlasOptions = {},
148: ): StormAtlasSummary {
149:   const list = entries ?? []
150:   const headlineBands = options.headlineBands ?? DEFAULT_HEADLINE_BANDS
151:   const headlineThresholdWords = options.headlineThresholdWords ?? DEFAULT_HEADLINE_THRESHOLD_WORDS
152:   const scenarioLabel = options.scenarioLabel ?? DEFAULT_SCENARIO_LABEL
153: 
154:   const counts = emptyBandCounts()
155:   for (const entry of list) {
156:     if (!entry || typeof entry !== 'object') {
157:       continue
158:     }
159:     counts[entryBand(entry)] += 1
160:   }
161: 
162:   // Total is the sum of the counts, so a defensively skipped row can

461: /**

463:  * and index it: ids sorted ascending by numeric value plus a Map for O(1)
464:  * selection. Every refusal names the field that broke the contract.

466: export function parseProfilesArtifact(raw: unknown): ProfilesArtifact {
467:   const root = asRecord(raw, 'profiles.json')
468:   requireExactKeys(root, ['meta', 'profiles'], 'profiles.json')
469: 
470:   const meta = parseMeta(root.meta)
471:   const profilesRecord = asRecord(root.profiles, 'profiles')
472: 
473:   const entries = Object.entries(profilesRecord)
474:   if (meta.account_count !== entries.length) {
475:     throw new Error(
476:       `meta.account_count must equal the profile count (${entries.length}), got ${meta.account_count}`,
477:     )
478:   }
479: 
480:   const profiles: Record<string, AccountProfile> = {}
481:   for (const [key, value] of entries) {
482:     if (!ACCOUNT_ID_PATTERN.test(key)) {
483:       throw new Error(`profiles key "${key}" must be an account id of digits`)
484:     }
485:     profiles[key] = parseProfile(key, value)
486:   }
487: 
488:   const ids = Object.keys(profiles).sort((left, right) => Number(left) - Number(right))
489:   return {
490:     meta,
491:     profiles,
492:     ids,
493:     byId: new Map(ids.map((id) => [id, profiles[id] as AccountProfile])),
494:   }
495: }

525: /**
526:  * Prefix matches first, then substring matches, over the sorted id
527:  * index. No fuzzy library: a judge types digits, so exact prefixes are
528:  * the useful order and an empty query returns nothing (the UI shows the
529:  * example id instead of a 4,500 row list).
530:  */
531: export function searchAccountIds(
532:   ids: readonly string[],
533:   query: string,
534:   limit = 8,
535: ): string[] {
536:   const needle = query.trim()
537:   if (needle.length === 0 || limit <= 0) {
538:     return []
539:   }
540:   const prefixes: string[] = []
541:   const substrings: string[] = []
542:   for (const id of ids) {
543:     if (id.startsWith(needle)) {
544:       prefixes.push(id)
545:     } else if (id.includes(needle)) {
546:       substrings.push(id)
547:     }
548:     if (prefixes.length >= limit) {
549:       break
550:     }
551:   }
552:   return [...prefixes, ...substrings].slice(0, limit)
553: }

102: }

104: /** Pull every piece of prose out of one source file. */
105: function proseOf(file: string, text: string): Prose[] {
106:   const prose: Prose[] = []
107:   let rest = text
108: 
109:   const push = (chunk: string, index: number, where: string): void => {
110:     prose.push({ file, line: lineOf(text, index), chunk, where })
111:   }
112: 
113:   // Block comments first, then line comments, so an apostrophe inside a
114:   // comment can never open a string that swallows real code.
115:   rest = rest.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, (chunk, index: number) => {
116:     push(chunk, index, 'block comment')
117:     return ' '
118:   })
119:   rest = rest.replace(/\/\/[^\n]*/g, (chunk, index: number) => {
120:     push(chunk, index, 'line comment')
121:     return ' '
122:   })
123: 
124:   const stringPattern = /'(?:[^'\\\n]|\\.)*'|"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"|`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g
125:   let match: RegExpExecArray | null
126:   while ((match = stringPattern.exec(rest)) !== null) {
127:     // Template expressions are code, not copy.
128:     const chunk = match[0].replace(/\$\{[^}]*\}/g, '')
129:     push(chunk, match.index, 'string literal')
130:   }
131:   rest = rest.replace(stringPattern, ' ')
132: 
133:   // JSX text nodes: prose between a tag close and the next tag open.
134:   const jsxPattern = />([^<>{}]+)</g
135:   while ((match = jsxPattern.exec(rest)) !== null) {
136:     const chunk = match[1] ?? ''
137:     if (PROSE.test(chunk) && /[A-Za-z]/.test(chunk)) {
138:       push(chunk, match.index, 'jsx text')
139:     }
140:   }
141: 
142:   return prose
143: }

250: /** Validate a parsed world.json payload against the documented schema. */
251: export function parseWorld(raw: unknown): World {
252:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'world')
253:   const meta = parseMeta(record.meta)
254:   const categories = asArray(record.categories, 'world.categories').map(parseCategory)
255:   const subscriptions = asArray(record.subscriptions, 'world.subscriptions').map(
256:     parseSubscription,
257:   )
258:   const splurges = asArray(record.splurges, 'world.splurges').map(parseSplurge)
259:   const incomeEvents = asArray(record.income_events, 'world.income_events').map(parseIncomeEvent)
260:   const balanceSeries = parseBalanceSeries(record.monthly_balance_series)
261:   const debtHorizon = parseDebtHorizon(record.debt_horizon)
262: 
263:   if (categories.length + subscriptions.length + splurges.length + incomeEvents.length === 0) {
264:     throw new Error('world must contain at least one entity')
265:   }
266: 
267:   // The generator announces its own counts; a mismatch means the file was
268:   // hand edited or two pipeline runs were spliced together.
269:   const counts = meta.entityCounts
270:   const actual = {
271:     categories: categories.length,
272:     subscriptions: subscriptions.length,
273:     splurges: splurges.length,
274:     income_events: incomeEvents.length,
275:     monthly_balance_series: balanceSeries.length,
276:   }
277:   for (const key of Object.keys(actual) as (keyof typeof actual)[]) {
278:     if (counts[key] !== actual[key]) {
279:       throw new Error(
280:         `world.meta.entityCounts.${key} must equal the emitted array length (${actual[key]}), got ${counts[key]}`,
281:       )
282:     }
283:   }
284: 
285:   return {
286:     meta,
287:     categories,
288:     subscriptions,
289:     splurges,
290:     income_events: incomeEvents,
291:     monthly_balance_series: balanceSeries,
292:     debt_horizon: debtHorizon,
293:   }
294: }

297: export const TRANSACTION_COLUMNS: readonly string[] = [
298:   'id',
299:   'date',
300:   'hour',
301:   'amountCents',
302:   'balanceCents',
303:   'type',
304:   'category',

308: function parseTransactionRow(raw: unknown, index: number): TransactionRow {
309:   const name = `rows[${index}]`
310:   if (!Array.isArray(raw)) {
311:     throw new Error(`${name} must be an array of ${TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length} values`)
312:   }
313:   if (raw.length !== TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length) {
314:     throw new Error(
315:       `${name} must have ${TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length} values, got ${raw.length}`,
316:     )
317:   }
318:   const type = raw[5]
319:   if (type !== 'debit' && type !== 'credit') {
320:     throw new Error(`${name}.type must be "debit" or "credit"`)
321:   }
322:   return {
323:     id: asString(raw[0], `${name}.id`),
324:     date: asString(raw[1], `${name}.date`),
325:     hour: asInteger(raw[2], `${name}.hour`),
326:     amountCents: asInteger(raw[3], `${name}.amountCents`),
327:     balanceCents: asInteger(raw[4], `${name}.balanceCents`),
328:     type,
329:     category: asString(raw[6], `${name}.category`),
330:     // The generator may emit an empty merchant when the source CSV has no
331:     // merchant_name column, so only the type is validated here.
332:     merchant: typeof raw[7] === 'string' ? raw[7] : asString(raw[7], `${name}.merchant`),
333:   }
334: }

336: /** Validate a parsed transactions.json payload against the documented schema. */
337: export function parseTransactions(raw: unknown): TransactionsFile {
338:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'transactions')
339:   const columns = asArray(record.columns, 'transactions.columns').map((column, index) =>
340:     asString(column, `transactions.columns[${index}]`),
341:   )
342:   if (columns.join(',') !== TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.join(',')) {
343:     throw new Error(
344:       `transactions.columns must be ${JSON.stringify(TRANSACTION_COLUMNS)}, got ${JSON.stringify(columns)}`,
345:     )
346:   }
347:   const rawRows = asArray(record.rows, 'transactions.rows')
348:   if (rawRows.length > MAX_TRANSACTION_ROWS) {
349:     throw new Error(
350:       `transactions.rows has ${rawRows.length} rows, above the ${MAX_TRANSACTION_ROWS} row cap`,
351:     )
352:   }
353:   const rows = rawRows.map(parseTransactionRow)
354:   const seen = new Set<string>()
355:   for (const row of rows) {
356:     if (seen.has(row.id)) {
357:       throw new Error(`duplicate transaction row id ${row.id}`)
358:     }
359:     seen.add(row.id)
360:   }
361:   return { columns, rows }
362: }

364: /** Base URL for bundled data assets (Pages subpath aware). */

372:   if (!response.ok) {
373:     throw new Error(`world.json fetch failed with status ${response.status}`)
374:   }

381:   if (!response.ok) {

383:   }

298:   'id',
299:   'date',
300:   'hour',
301:   'amountCents',
302:   'balanceCents',
303:   'type',
304:   'category',
305:   'merchant',
306: ]

308: function parseTransactionRow(raw: unknown, index: number): TransactionRow {
309:   const name = `rows[${index}]`
310:   if (!Array.isArray(raw)) {
311:     throw new Error(`${name} must be an array of ${TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length} values`)
312:   }
313:   if (raw.length !== TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length) {
314:     throw new Error(
315:       `${name} must have ${TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.length} values, got ${raw.length}`,
316:     )
317:   }
318:   const type = raw[5]
319:   if (type !== 'debit' && type !== 'credit') {
320:     throw new Error(`${name}.type must be "debit" or "credit"`)
321:   }
322:   return {
323:     id: asString(raw[0], `${name}.id`),
324:     date: asString(raw[1], `${name}.date`),
325:     hour: asInteger(raw[2], `${name}.hour`),
326:     amountCents: asInteger(raw[3], `${name}.amountCents`),
327:     balanceCents: asInteger(raw[4], `${name}.balanceCents`),
328:     type,
329:     category: asString(raw[6], `${name}.category`),
330:     // The generator may emit an empty merchant when the source CSV has no
331:     // merchant_name column, so only the type is validated here.
332:     merchant: typeof raw[7] === 'string' ? raw[7] : asString(raw[7], `${name}.merchant`),
333:   }
334: }

336: /** Validate a parsed transactions.json payload against the documented schema. */
337: export function parseTransactions(raw: unknown): TransactionsFile {
338:   const record = asRecord(raw, 'transactions')
339:   const columns = asArray(record.columns, 'transactions.columns').map((column, index) =>
340:     asString(column, `transactions.columns[${index}]`),
341:   )
342:   if (columns.join(',') !== TRANSACTION_COLUMNS.join(',')) {
343:     throw new Error(
344:       `transactions.columns must be ${JSON.stringify(TRANSACTION_COLUMNS)}, got ${JSON.stringify(columns)}`,
345:     )
346:   }
347:   const rawRows = asArray(record.rows, 'transactions.rows')
348:   if (rawRows.length > MAX_TRANSACTION_ROWS) {
349:     throw new Error(
350:       `transactions.rows has ${rawRows.length} rows, above the ${MAX_TRANSACTION_ROWS} row cap`,
351:     )
352:   }
353:   const rows = rawRows.map(parseTransactionRow)
354:   const seen = new Set<string>()
355:   for (const row of rows) {
356:     if (seen.has(row.id)) {
357:       throw new Error(`duplicate transaction row id ${row.id}`)
358:     }
359:     seen.add(row.id)
360:   }
361:   return { columns, rows }
362: }

364: /** Base URL for bundled data assets (Pages subpath aware). */
365: export function dataBase(): string {
366:   return import.meta.env.BASE_URL ?? '/'
367: }

369: /** Fetch and validate world.json. */
370: export async function loadWorld(): Promise<World> {
371:   const response = await fetch(`${dataBase()}data/world.json`)
372:   if (!response.ok) {
373:     throw new Error(`world.json fetch failed with status ${response.status}`)
374:   }
375:   return parseWorld(await response.json())
376: }

378: /** Fetch and validate transactions.json. */
379: export async function loadTransactions(): Promise<TransactionsFile> {
380:   const response = await fetch(`${dataBase()}data/transactions.json`)
381:   if (!response.ok) {
382:     throw new Error(`transactions.json fetch failed with status ${response.status}`)
383:   }
384:   return parseTransactions(await response.json())
385: }
